\title{Where Should Machine Learning Go in Hybrid Trading Systems?\\
Matched-Budget Component Attribution Across Five Strategies and \STwoInstruments{} Instruments}
\author{}
\date{Version 5 --- pre-registered, fully pipeline-generated results;
code, data, and tests: \url{https://github.com/Cannonbold2412/ML_Component_Attribution}}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Hybrid trading systems combine rule-based signals with machine-learned components, but rarely ask
\emph{at which decision point} ML adds value. We introduce Matched-Budget Component Attribution (MBCA):
hold data, features, model class, hyperparameters, freeze discipline, and evaluation fixed, and replace
one insertion point at a time --- regime filter, meta-labeling, position sizing, entry, or exit --- with a
matched-budget learned counterpart. Study 1 applies MBCA to one strategy in three markets
(\SoneSigGain{} significant improvements, \SoneSigLoss{} significant losses in \SoneConfigs{}
configurations). Study 2, pre-registered in version control before any data existed, applies it to five
historically documented strategies (JMA and dual moving-average crossovers, Donchian breakouts,
time-series momentum, RSI(2) mean reversion) on \STwoInstruments{} daily series across \STwoMarkets{}
asset-class markets from \STwoFirst{} onward, with two independent freeze dates, close-price stop
fills, per-market costs, mark-to-market portfolios, a paired block bootstrap, and false-discovery-rate
control. Of \STwoMktTests{} market-level tests, \STwoMktRawSig{} have raw $p<0.05$ but only
\STwoMktSigGain{} survive as significant gains and \STwoMktSigLoss{} as losses. Narrowing components
(meta-labeling, sizing) improve Sharpe in \STwoMktMetaPos{} and \STwoMktSizingPos{} of cells, are never
significantly harmful, and transfer across markets, but their effect is small and replicates only
partially across freezes. Replacing components are strategy-dependent: ML entry is the most harmful
component, while ML exit is the only one that significantly improves a strategy in several markets
(RSI(2), \STwoMktExitGainRSI{} significant gains). Execution realism dominates: stop-level fills
inflate the rule-based controls' Sharpe by \STwoExecBaseStopMin--\STwoExecBaseStopMax{}. Every
table, figure, and number is generated from the released pipeline.
\end{abstract}

\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} matched-budget component attribution, hybrid trading systems,
meta-labeling, pre-registration, reproducibility, walk-forward validation, block bootstrap,
false discovery rate, technical trading rules
